task: Hardening 2: fail loudly when a post or profile edit is not saved (HIGH-05); fixed-width migration prefixes + numeric sort (HIGH-04); schema.sql matches production and resets the migration stamp; setup runs migrate (HIGH-03)

context.create_activity: If the INSERT fails (for example, the Cognito user has no public.users row, which was the August incident class), query_commit returns None. The code then looked up activity None, got the string '{}', and the route answered 200. The post appeared to succeed but nothing was saved. It now returns errors ['activity_not_saved'], which data_activities in app.py must map to a non-200 status (phase-1 STOP 5 checks this; Claude has not yet seen that part of the route).
context.migration_prefix: str(time.time()).replace('.', '') drops trailing zeros, so about 24% of prefixes were shorter than 17 digits. A 16-digit prefix is roughly 10x SMALLER than the stored stamp 17800000000000001, so bin/db/migrate would skip it with no error. time.time_ns() // 100 always has 17 digits until 2286 (today it is about 1790...e16, above the hand-picked 17800000000000002 reserved for likes). The generator also refuses to create a prefix that is not greater than every existing one. migrate now sorts numerically.
context.schema: schema.sql lacked users.bio. After the hardening spec it already has the uuid reply_to_activity_uuid, so it creates the tables in their CURRENT shape. But its stamp row used ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with '0', so on a reused database the old stamp survived a reload. migrate would then either re-run folded migrations and fail ('column bio already exists') or skip real ones. Loading schema.sql now sets the stamp to 17800000000000001, the newest migration it contains, and bin/db/setup runs migrate afterwards to apply anything newer. Convention from now on: a new migration is ALSO folded into schema.sql, and the stamp value is bumped (the likes spec will be updated to do this).
context.tested: Claude ran these checks. In a real PostgreSQL 16, the edited schema.sql loads cleanly twice. A deliberately stale stamp ('0') is reset to 17800000000000001 on reload. users gains bio as its last column, matching production's column order. Re-running the bio migration fails with 'column "bio" already exists', which proves the stamp must skip it. The edited generator produced a 17-digit prefix above 17800000000000002 and refused when a larger prefix existed. The numeric sort orders 9_ < 1774... < 1780..., where a text sort would not.
context.edit_method: Exact find-and-replace; each 'old' occurs exactly once. Use the IDE file-edit tool.
context.update_profile: Found by Kiro while running the hardening spec. users/update.sql is UPDATE ... RETURNING handle. When it fails or matches no row (a Cognito user with no public.users row), query_commit now returns None. query_users_short(None) then returns '{}' and data_update_profile answered 200, so the profile page would say 'saved' when nothing was saved. The new check returns ['profile_not_updated']. Claude has read data_update_profile: it maps any non-None model['errors'] to 422.

# Fixed width (audit HIGH-04). str(time.time()) drops trailing zeros, so about
# 24% of prefixes came out shorter than 17 digits, compared SMALLER than the
# newest applied migration, and were silently skipped by bin/db/migrate.
# time.time_ns() // 100 (units of 100 ns) is always 17 digits until the year 2286.
timestamp = str(time.time_ns() // 100)

edits.id: GEN_B: generator: refuse a prefix that is not greater than every existing one
edits.new:
migrations_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(backend_dir, 'db', 'migrations', filename))

# Refuse to create a migration that would not run AFTER every existing one
# (for example after a hand-picked prefix such as 17800000000000002).
existing = [int(f.split('_', 1)[0]) for f in os.listdir(os.path.dirname(migrations_path)) if f.split('_', 1)[0].isdigit()]
if existing and int(timestamp) <= max(existing):
  print(f"ERROR: new prefix {timestamp} is not greater than the newest existing prefix {max(existing)}.")
  exit(1)

edits.id: MIG_A: migrate: sort by numeric prefix
edits.new:
migration_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(migrations_path, '*.py'))
# Sort by the numeric prefix, not as text (audit HIGH-04): text order and
# numeric order agree only while every prefix has the same width.
def _prefix(path):
  m = re.match(r'^(\d+)_', os.path.basename(path))
  return int(m.group(1)) if m else -1
migration_files.sort(key=_prefix)

edits.new:
-- This file creates the tables in their CURRENT shape: every migration up to
-- and including the prefix below is already folded in (users.bio, uuid

VALUES (1, '17800000000000001')
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET last_successful_run = EXCLUDED.last_successful_run;
